name: streamripper
why: Splits internet radio streams into tracks using Shoutcast metadata, a neat look at in-band title signalling.

brief.what_it_is: Streamripper is an open-source (GPL) command-line recorder for streaming MP3 radio. Its homepage says it lets you record streaming mp3 to your hard drive. You point it at an internet radio stream, and it writes the audio to disk. The scout note says it splits the recording into separate tracks using the Shoutcast title metadata sent with the stream, but the homepage itself does not describe the track splitting. The homepage also lists many front ends (GUIs and plugins) built on it.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit problem statement. It presents Streamripper as an application for recording streaming mp3 to a hard drive.
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to downloads on SourceForge and to a 'Supported Systems' page, which I did not open. It also mentions a Winamp plugin tutorial and a console tutorial, neither of which I read. The homepage gives no command-line install steps, accounts, or runtime requirements beyond the notes in the news (a glib dependency since 1.63.0, and a PCRE change in 1.64 beta).
brief.standout: Per the scout note, it reads Shoutcast in-band title metadata to cut a continuous radio stream into per-track files, which is a neat use of the stream's own signalling. The homepage's ecosystem of front ends, from Win32 to OSX to Java, is also unusual for a project of this size.
brief.status: quiet. The most recent news item on the homepage is dated 2008/10/14 (Streamripper 1.64 beta, with the forum closed to anonymous posting). The last released version named on the page is 1.63.0 (2008/05/04) plus a 1.64 beta. Several front ends are marked dead and unsupported. I found no later release date.
brief.caveats: The homepage is dated, with news ending in 2008. It says Windows 98 compatibility drove some of the glib and PCRE decisions. The forum moved to SourceForge and anonymous posting was disabled because of spam. Development was on CVS. Several listed front ends are explicitly 'dead' and unsupported. I did not read the docs or the 'How it works' page, so the track-splitting mechanism is unverified beyond the scout note.

fetch_log: https://streamripper.sourceforge.net/ - fetched OK; the page is a site index with news, not a README. No command lines appeared in it. I did not follow the Tutorial, FAQ, or 'How it works' links because the fetch returned their labels without URLs, and I did not guess URLs.
